findings.description: `recordedPanePids` always reads `conductor/pane-pid`, whether or not a conductor window is up, and no path ever removes that file. Once the conductor stops, crashes or the machine reboots, its old pid is a permanent match. If the OS later hands that pid to one of the operator's processes (their shell, terminal, sshd or tmux server), `pup respawn`, `unblock`, `kill --respawn` and `plan edit --rescope` all refuse, and `pup ui` goes read-only. `pup conductor stop` does not clear it.
findings.body:
**The conductor's pane-pid record is never cleared, and it is always read.**

`launchedAncestor` limits session records to `holdingStates()`, which bounds how long a dead window's pid can match. The conductor record gets no such limit. `recordedPanePids` adds it on every call:

```ts
[conductorPanePidFile(repoPath), conductorName(projectId(repoPath))],
```

The function's own JSDoc says "A record outlives its window: which windows may still be up is the caller's to choose", but the caller never gets that choice for the conductor. Nothing deletes the file either. `stopConductor` (`src/core/conductor.service.ts:229-231`) calls `killConductor` (`session-runtime.service.ts:977-985`), which only kills the tmux windows. The only thing that replaces the record is the next `launchConductor`.

**Trigger**
1. Run `pup conductor start`, then `pup conductor stop`. Letting the window exit or rebooting has the same effect.
2. The OS later hands the stored pid to a long-lived process that is an ancestor of the operator's `pup` call: their login shell, terminal, sshd or tmux server. After a reboot, pids are handed out from low numbers again.
3. `launchedAncestor` checks every pid against the recorded panes before the tmux-skipping `--name` check (`operator-guard.service.ts:56-59`). From then on, rescope, respawn, unblock and `kill --respawn` refuse, saying the caller is "under … pup-conductor-…'s window", and `pup ui` goes read-only.

ADR 0188 accepts pid reuse only for "a crashed pane on a blocked session", whose fix is "killing the session or ending that process clears it". A stopped conductor has no session to kill, and `pup conductor stop` does nothing about it. The only ways out are restarting the conductor so it overwrites the record, or deleting the file by hand.

**Fix:** read the conductor record only while `hasConductorWindow(projectId(repoPath))` is true. That also covers a conductor that exited on its own, and a reboot. Removing the file in `killConductor` only covers a clean stop.

findings.description: `pup merge` without `--pr`, and `--accept-debt` recorded as `human`, are held to the operator by the session and conductor markers alone. A worker or the conductor that empties them (`PUP_CONDUCTOR= pup merge <id> --accept-debt`) still fast-forwards the target, or writes a debt acceptance in the operator's name, under a recorded pane.
findings.body:
**`pup merge` is still guarded by forgeable markers only.**

Decision 188's premise is that the marker-only refusals of decisions 44 and 47 can be forged, because "the caller can empty or unset" them. The PR adds the process-tree check to rescope, respawn, unblock and `kill --respawn`. It also makes `pup ui` read-only under a recorded pane because "its keys run the respawn, the unblock and the merge" (`readOnlyUnderWindow`, index.ts:993-998). The CLI's own local merge still reads only the markers:

```ts
if (callingSession(db)) { return refuse(...); }
const conductor = callingConductor();
if (conductor && !opts.pr) { return refuse(...); }
if (conductor && opts.acceptDebt && !approvedBy) { return refuse(...); }
```

`launchedAncestor` has only two callers outside tests, `refusedUnderWindow` and `readOnlyUnderWindow`, and neither one is on this path.

**Trigger**
- The conductor runs `PUP_CONDUCTOR= pup merge <session>`. The gate still runs, but the target is fast-forwarded locally with no operator and no PR for the human to merge (decisions 47, 75).
- A worker leaves its worktree and runs `PUP_SESSION_ID= pup merge <id> --accept-debt <r> --review-by <d>`. Line 2550 records `acceptedBy: approvedBy ?? 'human'`, so the debt ledger says the operator accepted a debt it never saw.

The result is that the UI's merge key is guarded while the stronger CLI merge stays open. ADR 0188 never scopes merge out; the only exclusion it explains is plain `pup kill`. The same gap applies to `pup dashboard` (index.ts:1879-1886). Its `showAttachCommand` check is `!(callingSession(db) || callingConductor())`, so a window with emptied markers can start the server, read the token URL and POST answer, debt-close or land actions.

**Fix:** after the marker checks, call `refusedUnderWindow(db, repoPath, '`pup merge`')` whenever the call is the operator's alone, i.e. `!opts.pr || (opts.acceptDebt && !approvedBy)`, so the conductor's legitimate `--pr` path still runs. Either guard `pup dashboard` the same way, or state in ADR 0188 why these commands are left out.

findings.description: taskRescopes reads every `rescope` event on any session of the task, killed ones included, with no cutoff. So after a kill (killed is not a claimed state, so the task returns to the backlog), a plain `pup plan edit <task> --scope ...` that replaces scope-in (and maybe `--tier standard`), and a relaunch, the new session's PR body `## Rescopes` and its needs-you line still say `scope widened after launch: +<glob>` and `tier critical, raised from standard`. Those globs and that tier are no longer in the spec the gate checked. Possible fix: ignore rescope events older than the newest spec edit, or older than the first session launched after it.

`pup status` prints each inbox line through `sanitizeReason`, which keeps only the first 300 characters (src/cli/ui/dashboard-text.utils.ts:136). The new clause is added after a reason that can already be 107 characters ('CI review status reads clean ... merge click'), so a pr-open line with three rescoped globs of about 60 characters each loses the third glob and its '(+N more)' count without any marker. The operator still sees 'scope widened after launch' but not how far it was widened; the web dashboard escapes the line and does not cut it.

The comment "The rewrite replaces the whole body: the rescopes the first gate listed are read again..." restates the JSDoc of `sessionPullRequestText`/`pullRequestText` in merge-gate.service.ts; general.md §Comments seam-duplication rule says delete the call-site copy.

`pullRequestText` now has no production caller besides the new `sessionPullRequestText`, so two layers forward a long positional argument list; fold them into one function taking `db` and `session`, or mark `pullRequestText` as the test seam if that is why the split exists.

02-cli.md still says only "a session or the conductor gets the dashboard read-only"; after this change `pup ui` is also read-only for any caller under a recorded pane pid or an unreadable process tree, so a reader thinks unsetting the markers restores the controls. Point to decision 188.

ADR 0188's *The match* says each pid is checked against recorded panes, then against `--name`, but leaves out that the `--name` check skips tmux processes, which operator-guard.service.ts's docstring and decision 115 both state.
